To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) visual patterns can be used to infer the personality traits of users of a social media site, (ii) the personality traits inferred from visual patterns correlate significantly with the personality traits self-assessed and with the personality traits attributed by other users of the social media site.

the personality of a person can be inferred, with high accuracy, from the images he or she considers "favourite", and that the personality traits of a user can be inferred from his/her visual patterns, with accuracy comparable to the self-assessed personality.
the visual patterns of Flickr users are correlated with their personality traits to a statistically significant and meaningful extent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
unveiling the unconscious cognitive effects in multimedia and with developing new methods for multimedia content analysis that take them into account.
unveiling the implicit cognitive processes that shape our perception of multimedia content, as well as with developing new approaches that can take into account such processes.

the following questions: (1) How do we perceive the world and multimedia content in a non-conscious, automatic way?; (2) How can we measure such a perception?; (3) How can we take into account such a perception in multimedia content analysis
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the paper demonstrates that the implicit personality correlates of visual content can be inferred from a large number of pictures, and that this inference can also be used to improve the accuracy of the prediction of self-assessed and socially attributed personality traits.
the paper shows that there are visual features of the photos that are associated with the users' personalities.
, by using multimedia content analysis techniques and cognitive psychology findings, it is possible to infer implicit personality traits from multimedia content.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the unconscious is also a part of the multimedia unconscious.
the multimedia unconscious exists and it is possible to unveil it.
we can infer personality traits from visual content and vice versa.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, by taking into account implicit cognitive processes, we can unveil a new layer of multimedia content, thus improving the understanding of the media and the users.
multimedia data are not just a passive representation of the world but they also contain implicit cognitive processes that can be exploited to improve content analysis.
the cognitive effects of multimedia data are not a mere epiphenomenon.
